{{Short description|Manuscript in Ancient Greek}}
'''Papyrus Oxyrhynchus 90''' (P. Oxy. 90) is a receipt for the payment of wheat, written in [[Greek language|Greek]]. The manuscript was written on [[papyrus]] in the form of a sheet. It was discovered in the Egyptian city of [[Oxyrhynchus]]. The document was written between 179–180. Currently it is housed in the [[British Library]] (761) in [[London]].<ref name = Oxy>[http://163.1.169.40/cgi-bin/library?e=d-000-00---0POxy--00-0-0--0prompt-10---4----ded--0-1l--1-en-50---20-about-1708--00031-001-1-0utfZz-8-00&a=d&c=POxy&cl=CL5.1.1&d=HASH66d2209e4ce54c9e92ae08 P. Oxy. 90] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120529061554/http://163.1.169.40/cgi-bin/library?e=d-000-00---0POxy--00-0-0--0prompt-10---4----ded--0-1l--1-en-50---20-about-1708--00031-001-1-0utfZz-8-00&a=d&c=POxy&cl=CL5.1.1&d=HASH66d2209e4ce54c9e92ae08 |date=2012-05-29 }} at the Oxyrhynchus Online</ref> It is known also as  '''P. Lond. 3 p.&nbsp;XXXII no. 761'''.<ref name = LDAB>[http://www.trismegistos.org/ldab/text.php?tm=20749 P. Oxy. 1 90] [[LDAB]]</ref>

== Description ==
[[File:P.oxy.90.possible.cryptogram.png|thumb|The possible cryptogram from P. Oxy. 90]]

The fragment contains a receipt, and is similar to [[Papyrus Oxyrhynchus 89]]. It was written by an unknown author. It states  "that Clarus, ex-''[[agoranomus]],'' had deposited 8 ''artabae'' 4 ''[[Ancient_Greek_units_of_measurement#Volume|choenices]]'' in the public granary". According to [[Bernard Grenfell|Grenfell]] and [[Arthur Surridge Hunt|Hunt]], the last two lines are "written in Greek characters, but cannot be construed as Greek. Since they do not appear to be Graecized [[Demotic Egyptian script|demotic]], they are possibly a [[cryptogram]] of some kind." The measurements of the fragment are 103 by 80&nbsp;mm.<ref name = Grenfell>{{Cite book
 | last = Grenfell
 | first = B. P.
 | author-link = Bernard Pyne Grenfell
 | last2 = Hunt
 | first2 = A. S.
 | author-link2 = Arthur Surridge Hunt
 | title = Oxyrhynchus Papyri I
 | publisher = Egypt Exploration Fund
 | year = 1898
 | location = London
 | pages = 152–153
 | url = https://archive.org/stream/oxyrhynchuspapyr01grenuoft#page/152/mode/2up
 }}</ref>

It was discovered by Grenfell and Hunt in 1897 in Oxyrhynchus. The text was published by Grenfell and Hunt in 1898.<ref name = Grenfell/> The fragment was examined by [[Frederic G. Kenyon]] (1907), who attempted to decipher it to no avail.<ref name = LDAB/>

== Text ==
{{lang|grc-x-hellen|
: μεμέ(τρηκεν)(*) ἰς̣(*) τὸ δη(μόσιον) (πυροῦ) γενή(ματος) τοῦ διελ(θόντος) ιθ (ἔτους)
: Αὐρηλίων Ἀντωνίνου καὶ Κομμόδου
: Κ[α]ισάρων τῶν κυρίων (διὰ) σι(τολόγων)(*) λιβὸ(ς) τοπ(αρχίας)
: [Σ]ερύ(φεως)(*) τόπ(ων) Κλάρος Διδύμου ἀγορανομή(σας)
: [θ]έμ(α) ἀρταβαι(*) ὀκτο(*) χ(οίνικας) δ, (γίνονται) (πυροῦ) (ἀρτάβαι) η \χ(οίνικες) δ./ Διογ(ένης) σι(τολόγος) σεσημ(είωμαι).}}
